- [USER] User asked if George Washington had slaves.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] George Washington owned slaves, inherited his first slaves from his father at the age of 11, and owned over 300 slaves at the time of his death.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] George Washington began to question the morality of slavery and freed some of his slaves in his will.
- [USER] User asked why George Washington didn't free all of his slaves and who were the slaves he did not free when he died.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] George Washington did not free all of his slaves because it was common for slave-owning plantation owners to keep slaves as property and pass them down to heirs.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Washington was concerned about the economic loss from freeing all of his slaves, as they were a significant source of labor on his estate.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Washington freed some slaves in his will, which provided for the emancipation of enslaved persons who had served him for at least 30 years or who were above the age of 60.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The slaves freed by Washington were to be "bound to service" until the age of 26 for males and 24 for females.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Washington left 123 slaves in the custody of his wife Martha and instructed her to provide for them but not to free them.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] After Washington's death, Martha freed some of the slaves and kept others as inherited property.
- [USER] User asked when the slaves inherited by Martha were completely freed.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant does not have information on when the slaves inherited by Martha Washington were completely freed.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The legal process for freeing slaves was complex and often required going to court, which could be costly and time-consuming.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Martha Washington passed away in 1802, and many states had laws requiring freed slaves to leave the state within a certain period or risk re-enslavement.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Some slaves inherited by Martha may have been freed gradually over time or in accordance with the terms of her will.
- [USER] User asked if Martha may have intentionally kept some slaves to protect them from re-enslaving.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is possible that Martha Washington kept some slaves to protect them from re-enslavement due to laws requiring freed slaves to leave the state.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Owning slaves was a common practice at the time, and it is unclear what Martha's intentions were.
